Q: passing on geom_raster() breaks to geom_contour() A:

Use the breaks argument of stat_contour. You will have to calculate the density values first and then use the scale to derive the breaks, which you can then pass to the plot.

library(ggplot2)
library(metR)

p <- ggplot(faithfuld, aes(waiting, eruptions, z = density)) +
  geom_raster(aes(fill = density))

d <- layer_data(p)

#see https://stackoverflow.com/a/72518770/1412059
scale  <- scale_fill_continuous()
scale$train(range(d$z))
breaks  <- scale$get_breaks()

p +
  geom_contour(color = "white", breaks = breaks) +
  geom_text_contour(color = "white", breaks = breaks, skip = 0) +
  scale_fill_continuous(breaks = breaks)

Q: MSB4276: The default SDK resolver failed to resolve SDK "Microsoft.NET.Sdk" because directory did not exist A:

I had the following error on a local development Build application...

The NuGetSdkResolver did not resolve this SDK because there was no version specified in the project or global.json.

MSB4276: The default SDK resolver failed to resolve SDK "Microsoft.NET.Sdk" because directory "C:\Program Files\Microsoft Visual Studio\18\Professional\MSBuild\Sdks\Microsoft.NET.Sdk\Sdk" did not exist

error MSB4236: The SDK 'Microsoft.NET.Sdk' specified could not be found.

  • It was working before with Visual Studio 2022 installed, but later I installed 2026 without any of the .NET Build Tools for SQL Server Development.

  • It was auto-detecting the newer version of Visual Studio installed, and trying to use the MSBuild tools for 2026 (while ignoring the 2022 versions already installed).

  • The fix was to modify the existing 2026 installation and include the .NET SDK component.

Adding .NET SDK to VS 2026

Start the Visual Studio Installer and Update utility...

C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\setup.exe

Click the "Modify" button on the relevant Visual Studio instance as referenced in the error message...

Select the "Individual Components" tab and tick the ".NET SDK" component under the .NET heading...

Note: You can tick any relevant required .NET SDK's or .NET Framework SDK's used in the solution (if they are not already installed).

Click the "Install while downloading" or "Modify" button to begin installation.

After it has installed, restart the computer before recompiling the Visual Studio solution.

Q: How do I convert from YAML to JSON in Java? A:

A common approach is to use Jackson's YAML module. Read the YAML with YAMLFactory into a JsonNode, then write it back as JSON using ObjectMapper. It's simple and preserves the data structure well.
